checks: Verified original §§1–2, equations (1)–(2): the normalization keeps the free test as an explicit hypothesis, without asserting it for coupled fiber deformations.

Affine functions of both signs give equal Jordan mass and moments. The accepted coupling sends each extreme source point to itself, because any nonpoint law admits a coordinate split with distinct conditional barycenters in K. Mutual singularity prohibits mass on those identity rows.

A nonextreme boundary point is inside a nontrivial supporting segment, hence inside a maximal line facet in the plane. Supporting affine slack confines its martingale row to the closed facet; its endpoints carry zero target arclength. Countability and disjointness then give the full localization of both marginals.

Restricted martingale rows give zero mass, zero tangent moment, and hinge Jensen inequalities. Conversely, interpolating any facet restriction by convex piecewise-linear functions gives the facet test using the specified interior knots. Finite perimeter and boundedness justify summation; the zero-density case is included.

dependencies.hypotheses: The Jordan parts are finite nonnegative measures compactly supported on the boundary; their equal masses and all convex test inequalities give full martingale marginals with the positive part first.

overlap.comparison: Its proof has the same necessity geometry, but its accepted planar conclusion is for the affine-log reserve density at zero reserve and injective levels. It neither states the equivalence for general bounded Borel densities nor proves the facet conditions sufficient.
Confines compatible mixed martingale rows to support planes, without the arbitrary planar density equivalence, endpoint exclusion and converse.

readability: The converse proves the entire convex test class; it does not require extending every one-dimensional convex facet test to the plane.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The planar martingale localization and the converse facet-by-facet characterization are valid for arbitrary bounded Borel densities.
